Welcome
Our school is unique.
We are located in a picturesque part of the country surrounded by nature. Our school logo, the ‘Learning Oak’ is visible throughout the grounds and is central to our ethos.
Our children are unique.
Each continues to overcome personal obstacles, on a daily basis. Our school community provides the fertile soil for our children to develop, flourish and grow, equipped and prepared, for the challenges of life.
The Oak Tree visually represents the accomplishment, we want each pupil to achieve, by the time they leave our school. Our children are acorns, that require nourishment with knowledge and life experiences, in a nurturing environment, to stimulate strong growth and reach their full potential.
Our Vision
Our vision is to deliver an accessible, bespoke curriculum, to cultivate a sense of belonging, encourage a culture of discovery and promote personal growth and development.

British Values
Traditions. Customs. Heritages.
Pupil independence...
Pupils are supported to develop a sense of pride in themselves through praise and positive reinforcement. Academy staff provide activities to help pupils develop self-confidence, increase their self-esteem and provide pupils with experiences that allow them to explore language of feelings.
Pupils are actively encouraged to make their own choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. They are also encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are taught how to exercise them safely and appropriately.
In June 2014, the Prime Minister emphasised the important role that British values can play in education. In relation to this, how well a school promotes such values is an aspect of Ofsted’s inspection process.
At Compton Dundon School British values are promoted in much of what we do, during school assemblies, PSHE lessons, Tutor time activities and discussions as well as through the planning and delivery of our broad and balanced curriculum. Along with promoting British values we also feel it is important to actively challenge pupils, staff or parents who express views (including extremist) that are contrary to fundamental British values.
We aim to celebrate and experience the wealth of traditions, customs and heritages that make up British Life. As such we organize and take part in whole school events and celebration days for example Comic Relief, Harvest Festival as well as external trips to the theatre and other cultural events.
Make decisions together...
All school staff listen to, and encourage pupils to share their views and respect others and to talk about their feelings. Pupils are taught to listen carefully and with concern to each other, respecting the right of every individual to have their opinions and voices heard. Staff support pupils during decision making processes and provide activities that involve turn taking and working as a team. The pupils are given regular opportunities to reflect on their thoughts and debate ideas with regard to current events and news. Our curriculum encourages our pupils to respect public institutions and services. This is done by inviting a range of visitors into the school as well as visiting key places and buildings in the area.
Rewarding good behaviour...
Compton Dundon School enforces the importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school or the country. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind the laws and school rules, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when rules are broken. Visits from Police and Fire Services help reinforce this message.
To encourage and promote good behaviour, attitude and work, we have a token economy which is consistently followed throughout the school. We are committed to highlighting and praising pupil’s efforts. Praise is given informally, individually, during group work, in front of the whole class and the whole school. Pupils are rewarded not only for achievement in curriculum areas but for positive behavior.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance of those with Different Faiths and Beliefs.
Mutual respect, tolerance and politeness are at the heart of our values. Pupils learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect whatever differences there may be. Respect and understanding for different faiths and beliefs are enhanced through PSHE, Project Learning, International Cultures, assemblies, themed weeks, noticeboards and displays.
We provide opportunities for the pupils to visit places of worship and we actively encourage visitors from a range of communities and organisations into our school.

About Our School
Our specialist educational resource for learners age 5 to 14 years is designed to meet the needs of children and young people with Autism, as well as Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) conditions and associated behavioural difficulties. We are committed to safeguarding and our emphasis is on nurturing the individual child to enable them to achieve their full potential.
Our small, nurturing environment provides limited places. Education is delivered individually or in small groups of usually, three learners. Our highly skilled teachers and learning support assistants are passionate about developing young peoples’ knowledge, skills and education.

Our Proprietors & Ethos
Jon Lloyd & Richard Maynard
"We have a long background in SEN education having worked in different roles in schools across the South West throughout our careers. We have experienced first-hand how difficult the whole educational experience can be for pupils with specific needs as well as for their families, who have often experienced frustration regarding the lack of understanding for their child.
With this in mind we created Propel Education Ltd in 2018 and opened Compton Dundon School in January 2019 following a successful Ofsted pre-registration inspection" (full report can be found on this website).
The purpose of the school is to create a pupil-centred educational package that caters for each individual need. We are passionate about creating a school environment and learning experience that will first allow each pupil to feel comfortable and happy at school and then as a result be able to thrive and achieve their full potential.
Many pupils have certain phobias and anxieties surrounding school life, whether it be attending in general or certain aspects of school such as noise, social interactions, environmental issues, size of peer groups or specific elements of the curriculum such as PE or reading. We understand the need to work hard with parents/carers and other professionals as well as with the pupils to address individual difficulties and create a bespoke educational experience that aims to remove any anxieties and create an environment in which each individual can realise their potential.
We have built a dedicated, specialist staff team who support our wonderful pupils to achieve aspirational, personal and social outcomes. We have a range of facilities to provide students with the best educational experiences and learning opportunities. Our learning environment is calm, understanding, welcoming and safe. We are very keen to stay at the forefront of education and technological developments and are looking to improve further the educational experience through the continual improvement of facilities and introduction of state of the art IT such as Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality.
By promoting school involvement, securing personal development and academic achievement our goal is to thoroughly prepare each pupil for the next stage of their academic life and provide the skills and tools to ensure that future academic experiences can be successfully managed and completed.
We have high expectations of our students and celebrate their ongoing successes through positive rewards!

Careers
Careers Education at Compton Dundon School
At Compton Dundon School, careers education is an integral part of preparing our pupils for adult life. We recognise that many of our learners require additional time, structure and support to build confidence in themselves and their future. Our careers programme is therefore carefully planned to develop self-esteem, resilience, motivation and realistic aspiration, while promoting inclusion, equality of opportunity and independence.
Careers learning is embedded across the curriculum and wider school life. Pupils are supported to explore their strengths, interests and ambitions, while developing the employability and life skills they will need to thrive beyond school. Our approach reflects the individual needs of our pupils and is adapted to ensure learning is meaningful, accessible and relevant.
Compton Dundon School has committed to using the Gatsby Benchmarks, an internationally evidence‑based framework that defines high‑quality careers guidance for young people in England. Although ambitious, we feel the benchmarks are an appropriate framework for all our pupils.
The Headteacher and School Careers Lead assess our school's careers provision on a termly basis and we are pleased to show our most recent evaluation in the document (See Gatsby Benchmarks button)
As you can see, improvements have been made in all areas, with exception to those areas that are already graded at 100%. We strive to achieve as close to 100% for all Gatsby Benchmarks as much as we possibly can.
Careers Development in Key Stage 2
In Key Stage 2, careers education focuses on broadening horizons and challenging stereotypes. Pupils learn about different jobs and roles through assemblies, visitors to school and educational visits. They begin to develop key skills such as communication, teamwork and problem-solving, which form the foundation for employability later in their education. Early exposure to the world of work helps pupils understand that there are many possible futures open to them.
Careers Development in Key Stage 3
In Key Stage 3, careers education becomes more personalised and reflective. Pupils are encouraged to develop self-awareness and consider their interests, strengths and aspirations. Through assemblies, curriculum links, PSHE, Life Skills and engagement with visitors from a range of employment sectors, pupils learn how school subjects connect to real careers. They are introduced to local labour market information and begin to explore pathways such as further education, apprenticeships and vocational routes, supported by external careers guidance where appropriate.
Working with Employers and the Wider Community
We actively work with employers and external partners to enrich our careers provision. Visitors to the school provide talks, workshops, mentoring opportunities and real-world insights into different industries. Where appropriate, pupils are offered supported work-related experiences that help them understand expectations, develop confidence and build employability skills in a safe and structured way. Employers also play a key role in helping us challenge barriers such as stereotyping and supporting positive outcomes for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
Preparing for the Future
Our careers programme aims to support every pupil to move forward with confidence into the next stage of their education or training. By combining high-quality careers education, meaningful experiences and personalised support, we help our pupils develop the skills, attitudes and self-belief needed to become successful, independent adults and valued members of their community.ContactOur Careers Lead is Rebecca Wells

PSHE
PSHE
Our PSHE curriculum supports pupils’ understanding of themselves, their relationships and the wider world, helping them develop confidence, resilience and the skills needed for everyday life.
In KS2, pupils focus on emotional awareness, friendships, respect and healthy lifestyles. Topics include managing feelings, personal and online safety, growing and changing, money awareness and understanding rules, responsibilities and community life.
In KS3, PSHE builds on this foundation by exploring mental health and wellbeing, healthy relationships, consent, online behaviour, identity and personal responsibility. Pupils also develop greater awareness of risk, decision-making, citizenship and future pathways.

Maths
Maths
Our maths curriculum is designed to develop strong number fluency, mathematical reasoning and confidence. Learning is carefully sequenced to ensure pupils build secure knowledge and skills over time, with a clear focus on understanding, application and problem solving across KS2 and KS3.
In KS2, pupils develop secure foundations in place value, mental and written calculation, fractions, decimals and percentages. They explore shape, measurement and data, and are introduced to early algebraic thinking. Pupils are encouraged to reason mathematically, identify patterns and apply methods to a range of practical and real-life contexts.
In KS3, pupils deepen and extend their understanding of number, algebra, geometry and statistics. They work with equations, sequences, graphs, ratio, probability, area and volume, developing increasingly accurate and logical approaches to problem solving. Pupils are taught to explain their reasoning clearly, use appropriate mathematical language and make connections between different areas of mathematics.

English
English
Our English curriculum develops confident readers, writers and communicators through a carefully sequenced programme that builds knowledge, vocabulary and skills progressively across KS2 and KS3.
In KS2, pupils study a wide range of texts including traditional stories, modern fiction, poetry and non-fiction. They are taught grammar, spelling and vocabulary explicitly and apply these skills through writing such as narratives, reports and persuasive pieces. Reading lessons focus on comprehension skills including inference, prediction and summarising, alongside structured discussion.
In KS3, pupils develop more analytical and independent skills. They study more complex texts, including The Tempest by Shakespeare and selected Sherlock Holmes stories, exploring themes, language and writer’s intent. Writing becomes more structured and sophisticated, with continued emphasis on accuracy, vocabulary and confident expression through discussion and debate.

Computing
Computing
Our computing curriculum builds pupils’ digital confidence, creativity and understanding of how technology works. In KS2, pupils learn essential digital skills, including using software to create documents, presentations, images and simple media. They develop early programming skills using block-based coding, exploring sequencing, repetition and basic logic. They are also taught how to stay safe online and use technology responsibly.
In KS3, pupils deepen their understanding of computer systems, networks, websites and data. Programming becomes more advanced, introducing structured problem-solving and text-based coding. Pupils also learn about the appropriate and ethical use of AI, including how AI tools work, their benefits, their limitations and how to use them safely and responsibly. They continue to develop digital content, analyse information, explore cybersecurity and understand how computers process and store data. The curriculum prepares pupils for the digital demands of modern life and future pathways in computing and IT.

International Culture
International Culture
Our International Culture curriculum broadens pupils’ understanding of the world by exploring different countries, traditions and ways of life. In KS2, pupils learn about global geography, food, festivals, daily life and cultural values through a range of engaging topics. They compare countries with the UK, develop respectful curiosity and reflect on how people live, work and celebrate in different parts of the world.
In KS3, pupils deepen their cultural awareness by exploring global history, belief systems, arts, ethics and significant world events. They study how culture influences identity, communication and society, while examining the similarities and differences between nations. Pupils are encouraged to think critically, celebrate diversity and understand their place in an increasingly interconnected world.

Ofsted Reports
In May 2024 Compton Dundon School received its second full Ofsted inspection. This was a 3-day inspection with two inspectors performing lesson observations, deep diving into subject areas and conducting quality assurance checks.
We are pleased to report that Compton Dundon School was judged to be Outstanding in one area and Good in all other areas!
Here are just a few of the positive comments made by inspectors...
"Pupils feel happy and proud of their school."
"Pupils feel calm and nurtured by staff who know them and their families very well."
"The school has high expectations of the pupils."
"The behaviour of pupils is exceptional."
"Pupils’ behaviour demonstrates the pride they have in their school. They are respectful to staff, towards one another and to the environment."
"The school has established a love of reading for pleasure. Pupils read daily. They are enthusiastic about their books."
"Pupils attend well…they want to be at school."
"The school is ambitious for pupils to experience a range of trips and activities to build their social skills and interactions."
"Parents are hugely positive about the school and the impact on their children."
